problem: Consider the lamina that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,-x\le y\le x}.$ Given that the area of the lamina is $4$ square units, find the $x$-coordinate of its centroid.

activity_context.topic_title: Moments and Centers of Mass of Plane Laminas

feedback.problem: Consider the thin plate $D$ enclosed between the curve $x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}$ and the $x$-axis for $-2\le y\le 0.$ Given that the area of the plate is $\pi ,$ find the $x$-coordinate of its centroid.
feedback.worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/14c292e8a224b59c143d0e8a57d43b554ce298cd4f44fc2169f516d683e8c35a.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{4-{y}^{2}},\,-2\le y\le 0}
$$

and ${A}_{D}=\pi .$

Therefore, the $x$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}\frac{4-{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}4-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{[4y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[0-(-8+\frac{8}{3})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\cdot \frac{16}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
